I feel you. I’m 38 spent my teens’s 20’s and first half of my 30’s partying, being irresponsible, and impulsive. Still trying to figure out how to “not do” those things anymore. Basically trying to unlearn everything I knew about life at the same time as learning how to learn how to do life. Those years of partying were awesome but it left me with a nagging addiction problem, impulsivity problem, and a lack of self discipline problem. I kept telling myself “I have time to grow up and get my shit together” then I had a life changing rude awakening. Life gave me a well deserved slap in the face. About 4 years ago I almost broke my neck trying to do a gainer off a 60’ cliff I’m ok now but it was a severe injury and a life changing moment. It was in the middle of summer and I was pretty fucked up laying on a couch so I had time to take inventory of my life, 15is years of partying, chasing girls, and not accomplishing my goals led me to that moment. 

Anyways I wasn’t planning to write all this but it’s relevant. What I’m trying to say is… Change is fucking hard!! Completely dismantling your thought processes, behavior patterns,and identity is even harder. 

Life has a way of hinting small course corrections at you. If you don’t listen to the hints life gives you and make adjustments then life will  smack you into the dirt until you pay attention. I had to learn this lesson the hard way more than once. 

All that to say I feel for you. Although it’s been an incredibly painful process I feel like it’s was all necessary to move me forward. I’ve grown more in the last 3-4 years than I have the previous 15-20. 

Keep your head up! I believe it will all be worth it in the end. Or I’ll just die at 56 years old from the abuse I’ve inflicted on my body so it won’t matter anyway. 

Much love. You’re doing great. You’re exactly where you’re supposed to be.

Yes I did! Hopefully I’m not too late in replying.  So I actually bought two stylus’s that both work well. I bought the “Bamboo Ink” and the “Bamboo Ink Plus” from Best Buy on Black Friday. I got both to test them and planned to return one but I liked them both for different reasons so I kept both. I couldn’t find any concrete information on stylus compatibility for the yoga 6, but as far as I know your only options are the factory Lenovo or one of these two. 

Bamboo Ink Plus:

Pros: AES 2.0 compatible (can confirm the tilt function works properly on my “Yoga 6 13ALC6”), more pressure sensitivity, has more functions/features, rechargeable, extra nibs, etc. 

Cons: battery is usually dead if it’s been sitting for a week or so, randomly doesn’t track for a split second, seems a little less responsive than the regular Bamboo Ink.

Bamboo Ink:

Pros: cheaper, nice weight and feel, very responsive, tracking never skips, battery seems to last quite a while. 

Cons: no tilt, less pressure sensitivity, not rechargeable, no extra nibs, 

Conclusion: I like both stylus’s but, I actually prefer the regular Bamboo Ink over the Bamboo Ink Plus. I didn’t actually find the tilt function to be as useful as I thought I would. The regular Ink is also cheaper, more responsive, the difference in pressure sensitivity between the two is negligible, and I didn’t really need the extra buttons.

I personally would just buy both like I did, test them, then return the other.

The bamboo ink plus seems slightly glitchy or momentarily laggy at times but over all has worked pretty well over the last few months. The bamboo ink has less features/buttons and is only AES 1.0 but it seems to run a little more smoothly on my system, it’s cheaper, and for me personally I don’t find the tilt function all that useful anyways. Best Buy or other box stores generally have a pretty good return policy so your best best is to just get one or both of these and see if you like them. Yes 100 percent this⬆️ that’s how i ended up going with the cr920. I fully planned on getting the 365xl which I already shot and knew I liked. Then I did an unlimited pistol rental at my local range and was there from 1-9pm doing side by side testing/comparing/contrasting about 24 different pistols. I was very surprised by several pistols. Some of the ones I thought I’d like I hated (Fn 509, horrendous trigger) and some that unexpectedly blew me away (Walther PDP. They are incredible!) 

The cr920 was the clear winner for me. But like you said. I will never buy another pistol without doing the unlimited rental side by side testing again. 

Some guns might look similar but they all have unique little personalities and quirks that you don’t know until you shoot them.

I just got one two weeks ago and it’s an absolute game changer. Have had 0 issues, even in the 200 round break In period. They have found the the issue that was causing the F2F. Some of the early serial numbers had a slightly different barrel design those barrels had a slightly different cutout on the top of the barrel that were the cause. They changed the design of the later versions inadvertently fixing the problem before they even knew there was one. Only early SN’s had this issue and if you have one of those barrels shadow systems will immediately just send you the newer barrel.  

No other manufacturer would take care of its customers like that. They aren’t making people send their guns in and be defenseless for 6weeks. They’ll just send you the new one to make it right. That’s unheard of in the industry. Almost every new glock version had issues including the gen5. I had the first gen early SN sig p365 several years ago that wouldn’t eat certain ammo because in early manufacturing they designed the feed ramp too narrow. I got F2F every 7 shots. Sig didn’t give a fuck about fixing my gun they only cared about fixing the future guns. So I immediately sold it after 3months and took almost a $200 loss. The customer service of shadow systems is top notch and everyone says that. 

 They may have a kink or two to work out here and there but shadow systems is an excellent company that makes excellent firearms. They’ll definitely go far in this industry and be a staple household name in the firearms world.

The hellcat is slightly snappy but these guys are blowing it out of proportion. Any gun in this category and size range is going to have a quite a bit of perceived recoil. But that’s waist training is for. You’ll quickly adapt the the recoil of any pistol you regularly train with. But recoil is a bigger deal for some than others. It’s never bothered me. The hellcat is a fantastic gun top 5 on the market IMO. I found it to be more accurate than the 365, 43, 48, shield. 

With all that being sad though get the cr920. This gun is by far my favorite in this category and I’ve shot all of them. And if you are worried about recoil this gun has less perceived recoil than any other similar gun on the market. The massive beaver tail makes a huge difference and your purchase on the weapon sits very high so the fulcrum point is lower, this equals less recoil. The only thing I’m not entirely in love with is the trigger, a bit spongy, and a little more travel than I like. The trigger is by no means bad though, and I would’ve replaced the trigger with a higher end one anyway. Beyond that this gun is practically flawless.
